question: What does in-guest tool-RCB bracketing COST versus the ptrace tracer? Specifically: is an in-guest RCB counter read a read() syscall or an rdpmc, how many ns and how many RCBs does each cost, and does the S1(b) ~31x trap-round-trip win survive after paying two bracket reads per tool callback?
author: hermit-e9patch (opus-4.8)

repos.reverie_note: The C microbench is standalone (no reverie linkage). reverie SHAs are cited only as the source of the attrs/event/read-path this tool MIRRORS: perf.rs:200-221 (attrs), timer.rs:64 (event 0x5100d1), perf.rs:337-360 (read() path), perf.rs:420-430 (index!=0 fallback).

tool.attrs: exclude_kernel/guest/hv=1, pinned=1, per-tid (pid=0), cpu=-1, sample_period=0 (counting), mmap page for fast reads — mirrors reverie perf.rs Builder::create

cgroup.note: 1-CPU cgroup isolates the read-primitive cost; axis (a) sequentialization = 0 (single thread), matching the S1(b) microbench isolation. Shared 316-CPU box; pinned=1 EOF-detects any deschedule and aborts, so a corrupt number cannot silently pass.

runtime_check.sanity_syscall_vs_rdpmc_delta: 4-5 RCB (agree; rdpmc seqlock impl validated correct)

method: Two-point slope ns/read = (median(T(Nb)) - median(T(Na)))/(Nb-Na), reps=20 + 2 discarded warmups; removes fixed per-call loop overhead. RCB self-cost measured with a SECOND 0x5100d1 counter bracketing a primitive loop minus an empty-loop baseline. 3 independent cgroup runs.

verdict.conclusion: In-guest tool-RCB bracketing is cheap-by-construction. The ~31x S1(b) trap-round-trip win SURVIVES under BOTH read primitives (~20x with read() fallback, ~30x with rdpmc). rdpmc is available and correct on this host and makes bracketing essentially free. RCB self-cost is a small constant (6 RCB per rdpmc bracket pair, 12 per read() pair) and thus trivially deductible, confirming the design's clean-baseline premise. FEASIBILITY: unified in-guest patching backend is not gated by accounting cost.

scope_caveats: Measures accounting/bracketing overhead ONLY. Does NOT measure axis (a) sequentialization (park + RPC to global scheduler) — backend-independent, degenerate on single-thread, excluded by design.

845.7 ns Mode A baseline is an UPPER BOUND (carries strace per-hook I/O); a bare null hook is faster, so bracketing is a larger FRACTION of a bare hook — but the absolute ns vs 26us ptrace is what the verdict rests on.

Rare cases (RCB overflow during record/replay; live single-step-to-exact-count fallback, timer.rs:800-856) are costed as design gaps in the landed design doc, NOT measured — no in-guest driver exists yet.

reverie does NOT implement rdpmc anywhere; its fast-loop falls back to read() when index!=0 (perf.rs:420-430). An in-guest rdpmc primitive would have to be ADDED (data-justified follow-up). reverie-liteinst cannot even reach PerfCounter (perf is a private mod; tool_host.rs:616-638 returns Unsupported for read_clock).
Host-scoped to this AMD Turin box (family 0x1A, skid-margin 1000, pmc_width 48).
